chapter: Breakup of Hines band to Lefty Bates
title: The Rum Boogie and its floor shows
summary: Smaller version of the Grand Terrace.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What happened after Fuller? With you?
With me? Well, there was still a small combo. After that -- oh, yeah,
After Fuller I went in the Rum Boogie, that's right. Because that was - what was that, '42?
Yeah, went in the Rum Boogie with Marl Young. And then went back in the Rum Boogie with Captain Walter Dyett.
Was the Rum Boogie sort of like the Grand Terrace?
Now, the Grand Terrace had a big influence on South Side clubs?
What were some of the acts that you played in the parties? Recall any?

Yeah, there was Barry Ruz (PHONETIC), and who the heck else was there? Oh, the dance act, called it The Lightning Flashes. I can't think -- oh, I can't think what the single acts were. There were still a lot of good acts in Chicago.
